body:
mina: Quick flag from support: new devs hitting confusing outputs in sample apps. Go prints "auth failed" on a 403, JS sample shows a raw stack. Folks aren't sure whether to re-auth or request scopes.

kevin: Oof. That's classic onboarding churn. We should standardize intent names and provide one short user-facing line + a fix suggestion.

alexa: Suggestion: pick canonical intents: authn, authz, rate_limit, conflict. SDKs expose typed errors named AuthenticationError, PermissionDenied, RateLimitError, ConflictError (language-idiomatic casing allowed).

priya: Important: the user-facing message must be a single concise sentence and one actionable hint. e.g. "Permission denied: missing scope 'inference.write'. Grant this scope or use a key with that role."

mina: Also: sampleapp README should include the exact message we expect users to see and a copy-paste CTA. Right now it dumps the full trace which scares folks.

kevin: Telemetry: emit error_intent and standard_error_code in logs so ops can alert on intent spikes. Keep original upstream body as raw_event for debugging.

alexa: Implementation notes for SDKs: simple deterministic mapper in HTTP layer. Pseudo: 
```
if status==401: raise AuthenticationError('token expired — refresh and retry')
elif status==403: raise PermissionDenied("missing scope 'inference.write'")
elif status==429: raise RateLimitError('quota exceeded — backoff', retry_after)
elif status==409: raise ConflictError('write conflict')
else: raise ApiError('upstream error')
```

priya: Quickstart friction: we auto-create keys with read-only perms by default. New users hitting write examples get 403s immediately. Options: broaden first-run scopes or change quickstart to call a read-only example by default and show how to enable write scopes.

mina: UX decision: what should the hosted API normalize? If an upstream service returns 403 with body {"reason":"quota"}, should API translate to 429 intent? I vote yes, as long as trace_id + raw body are kept.

kevin: Security fine with normalization if we store raw payload & add provenance headers.

alexa: Tests: SDK unit tests should assert both the typed exception and that the public message includes the hint token (refresh/check scope/backoff).

priya: I'll draft a short docs page with a mapping table (HTTP | intent | SDK type | user text | telemetry key) and a sampleapp patch showing how to catch and display the errors in JS/Python/Go.

devex-bot: Ticket created: DEVEX-2917 "Standardize SDK error intents + onboarding copy" assigned to @priya, @alexa. https://tickets.example/DEVEX-2917 :white_check_mark:

mina: Thanks everyone. If we land this we should see fewer basic support tickets within two sprints.
